video_title: The Knicks embody Kobe's MAMBA MENTALITY 🐍 - Danny Green is impressed with New York | SportsCenter

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on Knicks' Mamba mentality and hunger
quotes.excerpt: They're not satisfied. They're still hungry. They're taking on and embodying that Kobe Mamba mentality.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: Danny, I just went through the numbers for the Knicks, but which one is the most impressive to you?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: All the numbers are impressive. They're doing an unbelievable job of staying focused and locked in. That's the most impressive thing to me is their mindset, right? They're not satisfied. They're still hungry. They're taking on and embodying that Kobe Mamba mentality, right? They flipped the switch somewhere in the playoffs, which most people don't predict. Early in the season, I was like, they don't look together, they don't look like they're cohesive. But in that Atlanta series, they had somehow find a way to flip a switch and turn it on and then have not turned it off since. And even when they're up 3-0 or up 30 points, they're not satisfied and looking forward or looking ahead like, oh, we're in the finals or we're in the championship. Their expectation is a lot higher and again, they're showing that they're hungry and not satisfied even when they're up big in games.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green favors Knicks to win NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: Actually, they're my favorites to win it right now. The way the West is going and how they're battling out.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: We know what's coming up next. Quickly, how much of a chance do you give the Knicks against the Spurs or Thunder in the finals?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: Actually, they're my favorites to win it right now. The way the West is going and how they're battling out, they're beating each other up. They don't seem 100% healthy, especially OKC. San Antonio has some injuries, some guys banged up, but they're playing on those injuries. And even through the regular season when you've seen that San Antonio's matched up with the Knicks throughout the in-season cup final, they were struggling with them. That double big matchup gives Wemby some troubles. And when OKC, if they're down J-Dub or AJ Mitchell, it's hard to create offense with those guys being out. And the Knicks are so deep with Shamet, Deuce McBride, those guys come off the bench. I like the Knicks to be the favorites in this final series, whoever comes out of the West.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green on Cavaliers' necessary offseason changes to compete
quotes.excerpt: If you want to be a championship team, you have to compete with the New York Knicks.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: Let's get to the Cavs because they get embarrassed in the conference finals, Danny. What work do they need to do this offseason?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: A lot needs to happen, a lot needs to change. They had a great season, big picture, and I love what they did. They got to the Eastern Finals, but you can't be satisfied, right? So you got to make changes now. If you want to be a championship team, you have to compete with the New York Knicks. You have to compete with Oklahoma City Thunder and the San Antonio Spurs. So that means you got to find the right pieces around you, around Donovan Mitchell, whoever you keep on board. I like Donovan Mitchell and Evan Mobley to keep. Everybody else expendable. But you got to find three and D wings, some young athleticism, some guys, some bigs that can help you and compete with the New York Knicks, to compete with the San Antonio Spurs, Oklahoma City Thunder. So they got to find a roster and whatever else they make decisions wise, front office or coaching wise, to be able to be at the highest level and be contention. But all in all, they had a great season, but it's time to make moves and get better this summer.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim McMahon updates on Jalen Williams and AJ Mitchell's injuries
quotes.excerpt: AJ Mitchell out again. He has not been ruled out for the series, but the typical recovery time from a calf strain tells you that his return for the West Finals is pretty unlikely at best.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: Tim, let's start with those Thunder. Their offense Game 4, awful. They scored just 82 points in large part, no Jalen Williams and the AJ Mitchell's injuries. What more can you tell us about their availability tonight?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Howdy partners. AJ Mitchell out again. He has not been ruled out for the series, but the typical recovery time from a calf strain tells you that his return for the West Finals is pretty unlikely at best. Now, Jalen Williams is questionable once again, just like he was the previous two games. He missed both those games, was officially ruled out 45 minutes before tip-off after going through what were pretty light pre-game warm-ups, basically spot shooting sessions. Now, there was a change in his injury designation. They had been listing him with left hamstring soreness. That is now left hamstring injury management with a strain. And basically, it's an acknowledgment of what was obvious. He aggravated the strain that he suffered in the second game this postseason.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Danny Green advises Thunder to create offense from defense
quotes.excerpt: They got to create offense with their defense. Get easy baskets, get out on transition, get out and running.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: So Danny, how can OKC generate more offense if two of their best off-dribble creators are sidelined?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: They got to do what they've been doing and what they've been done for the last couple years. That's create offense with their defense. They got to be active, they got to get deflections, they got to get into people, be intense and be physical and not turn the ball over, which will help, so they get more shots on goal. But they got to create offense with their defense. Get easy baskets, get out on transition, get out and running, get some open looks for the young guys with Caruso and Cason Wallace and Jaylen McCan, even Jalen Williams, big Jalen Williams, to knock down threes. It's easier to get uncontested looks when you're in transition. And also you don't have a set defense of the Spurs and Wemby at the rim when you get transition. So they got to continue to do what they've always done in their DNA is be physical and create offense with their defense. So if they do that, they give themselves a chance. And if they take care of the ball, even better chance of them to win at home.

quotes.speaker: Michael C. Wright
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael C. Wright on Popovich's fiery speech changing Spurs' mindset
quotes.excerpt: He basically told them, hey, this is BS. We're not playing San Antonio Spurs basketball.

text_blocks.speaker: Host
text_blocks.text: Joining the party now is our NBA reporter Michael C. Wright, who is covering the Spurs. All right, Michael, San Antonio had a complete 180-degree turnaround after Game 4 after Greg Popovich had some choice words for the Spurs after Game 3. How did Pop help set the tone for the series moving forward?

text_blocks.speaker: Michael C. Wright
text_blocks.text: Well, let me tell you this about Pop. CEO RC Buford told me that Pop is at his best during the darkest days. Well, after Game 3, those were dark days. They had basically been punked by the Oklahoma City Thunder. And basically, Pop came into the locker room for the first time all season. All the players were there, the staff, GM Brian Wright, everybody was there. And he basically told them, hey, this is BS. We're not playing San Antonio Spurs basketball. So that whole speech was about recalibrating the mindset going into this whole thing because look, the Spurs had just come off a 60-win regular season and Pop was like, is this how you guys want to go out? Well, obviously, that's not the case. They do not want to go out that way. They want to come out on top. So just a mindset change and it was beneficial for the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4.
